measurement_notes: Single-threaded scalar reference path; no accelerated kernel exists for 50 to 60-bit moduli.
Raw harness runs stay under the ignored dist/zk-resource-harness/; only this summary is tracked.

The host ran other builds during the runs; the recorded system load is part of each run. Each configuration ran several times; run_spread gives the fastest and the slowest, and every derived time uses the run with the median evaluation time.
Cache policy: every run is a fresh process that builds its transforms and keys itself; no table, key or proof artifact is cached between runs, so warm describes the file cache of the binary only.

The batching comparator uses 60-bit main primes against the 50-bit primes of the candidates: at t = 786433 a product of two values at the rounding floor is about 87 bits, which one 50-bit prime per multiplication cannot bring back.

proof_work_projection.execution_relation_layout: one constrained residue multiplication per model work unit of the evaluation; a relation that batches or amortizes transforms would be smaller, and one that covers the padded maximum shape for every tape would be larger
proof_work_projection.input_relation_layout: Layout assumed (task R.11 selects the real one): the witness is the ternary mask u, the errors e0 and e1 and the slot scalars. Per main prime the relation transforms u, multiplies point-wise by the two public-key components and transforms both products back (three transforms and 4N further residue multiplications), then checks c0 = b*u + t*e0 + m and c1 = a*u + t*e1 coefficient-wise with one small quotient each. The plaintext is tied to its slots by one inverse slot transform modulo t. Every residue multiplication is range-checked through a quotient and a remainder in 16-bit limbs.
proof_work_projection.limb_model: 16-bit limbs over a 64-bit proof field as in the design memo: a residue below 2^62 is four limbs, a product of two residues is 16 limb products, and its quotient and remainder are range-checked limb by limb
proof_work_projection.status: projection only: no input, execution or opening proof exists (tasks R.11, R.3, R.7, R.8)

scope: Cost model and host measurements of the RNS-BGV starting candidates. It qualifies no profile, establishes no security level and grants no runtime permission.

security_estimate.core_svp_sanity: primal uSVP on the largest modulus Q*P with error sigma = sqrt(10.5) and a ternary secret, geometric series assumption, 2016 estimate. Reported: the block size beta, the core-SVP exponents 0.292*beta (classical) and 0.265*beta (quantum), and 0.292*beta + 16.4 + log2(8*d) in the style of the BDGL16 reduction cost model. Not a substitute for the Lattice Estimator: no dual, hybrid or algebraic attack is costed. The estimator block compares these numbers with its own primal uSVP result for every profile.

design_target.source: the task C.3 design memo: at least 128 classical bits under BDGL16 reduction costs, quantum costs reported separately; the verdict under ADPS16 (core-SVP) is reported beside it

tape_lowering.instruction_cost_basis: the costliest instance of each opcode in a tape that executes every opcode of the class once on operands loaded at the top level; copies, constants and plaintext additions cost no work unit
tape_lowering.level_policy: Lazy. A value stays at its level until an operation needs otherwise. A binary operation switches the operand at the higher level down to the level of the other. Before a product both operands are switched down one prime at a time while that strictly increases the ratio of the level capacity to the bound of the relinearized product (compared exactly); a squaring switches its operand once. A linear operation never gains capacity from a modulus switch, so this policy fits the longest chains of linear operations; it keeps values at high levels, which makes the charged work an upper estimate. It is the costing policy of the harness, not a schedule a consumer has adopted.
tape_lowering.lowering: Every register and state lane holds one scalar broadcast to all slots; registers start as the noiseless embedding of zero and lanes as the noiseless embedding of their initial scalars, at the top level. LoadInput multiplies the packed input by the idempotent of its slot and applies, for each broadcast element, the automorphism and an addition. LoadState and StoreState copy. LoadConst is the noiseless embedding at the top level. Add aligns and adds. AddPlain and SubPlain add or subtract the constant polynomial; MulPlain multiplies by it. Mul is one lowered product. SelectEqZero is eight lowered squarings of the condition, a lowered product with the embedded one, indicator = 1 - c^256, delta = zero - nonzero and nonzero + indicator * delta. Output multiplies by the idempotent of the next output slot and adds to the accumulator. At the end the accumulator is multiplied by the mask that zeroes every unused output slot.
tape_lowering.sanitization_projection: A projection of noise flooding, not a construction: with E = ceil(V / t), a uniform flood of half-width F = H * N * E * 2^kappa on every error coefficient hides a shift of 2E per release at statistical distance 2^-kappa over H releases, and the flooded, re-randomized output has the bound V + t*F + V_fresh. H and kappa are illustrative parameters nobody has selected. Flooding alone does not hide the second ciphertext component; the construction and its proof are task R.11.
tape_lowering.working_bytes_basis: peak_persistent_ciphertext_bytes is the residues of the input, the four registers, the 32 lanes and the output accumulator at an instruction boundary. peak_working_bytes adds the temporaries named in the harness and the tensor and key-switch scratch of one operation. Evaluation keys are not included.
